paleobiology.predecessor: none in this chronoseries; sympatric surface morph is the same-age comparison for pigment amplitude
paleobiology.scale_predecessor: smaller than 666 nm is not in this slot; the larger-scale sibling is the 24 um cellular wavelength (2.418e-5 m), ratio 36.328

law.name: Turing Reaction-Diffusion Wavelength Selection

equations.activator: du/dt = Du laplacian(u) + gamma (a - u + u^2 v)
equations.inhibitor: dv/dt = Dv laplacian(v) + gamma (b - u^2 v)
equations.growth: sigma(k) = largest real eigenvalue of gamma J - k^2 diag(Du, Dv)
equations.k_c: argmax_k sigma(k), calibrated so 2*pi/k_c equals 6.656e-7 m

law.boundary_conditions: periodic on the patch (Fourier pseudo-spectral). The whole-fish photograph is a mask for visualization only.

reported_in_source: Turing (1952) gives the diffusion-driven instability and a critical wavenumber.
Schnakenberg (1979) supplies the two-species kinetics used as the carrier.
Jeffery (2009) reviews regressive evolution of eyes and pigment in Astyanax cavefish.
Protas et al. (2006) map cavefish albinism to oca2; Gross et al. (2009) map reduced melanin to mc1r.
Yamamoto, Stock and Jeffery (2004) show Hedgehog-dependent lens apoptosis, not a pigment Turing mode, causes eye degeneration.
Yoshizawa et al. (2010) tie expanded superficial neuromasts to a feeding-behavior shift.
McCauley, Hixon and Jeffery (2004) place pigment-cell regression late in melanogenesis.
empirical_claims.not_reported_at_666_nm: No cited paper measures a 666 nm Turing wavelength on Astyanax skin. The length is the slot scale. The photograph cannot resolve it.
